effects: Sets `to` as the single approved address for the signer's PUT position NFT `tokenId`. That address can then transfer the position, along with the collateral and FT claims tied to it. (ERC721Upgradeable.approve -> _approve: $._tokenApprovals[tokenId] = to)
If `to` is the zero address, the existing approval for that position is cleared.
Moves no tokens or ETH. The function is not payable.
formats.shown: "Approve PUT pFT NFT #141", with the Operator address and the position NFT shown as fields.

findings.title: approve: interpolatedIntent leaves out the operator, though the sentence could carry the address.
findings.evidence: descriptor: "interpolatedIntent": "Approve PUT {tokenId}". The `to` field is shown as 'Operator' but is not in the sentence. Case 0 renders "Approve PUT pFT NFT #141" and does not say who gets control.

findings.title: approve: a zero-address operator means revoke, but the screen still reads 'Approve'.
findings.evidence: ERC721Upgradeable._approve stores $._tokenApprovals[tokenId] = to, so to=0x0 clears the approval. The descriptor has no handling for the zero address on the `to` field, so the screen shows 'Approve FT PUT position' with Operator 0x000…0.
findings.fix: Make the intent neutral, e.g. "Set FT PUT position approval", or label the field 'Approved address (0x0 = revoke)'.

findings.title: approve: Operator address `types` is limited to contract, but the code accepts any address, including an EOA.
findings.evidence: descriptor: to.params.types ["contract"]. ERC721Upgradeable.approve puts no limit on `to`. Case 0 approves an EOA (0xd8dA…6045).

effects: Grants or revokes (`approved`) `operator` control over every PUT position NFT the signer holds now or later. With control, the operator can transfer any of them. (ERC721Upgradeable._setApprovalForAll: $._operatorApprovals[owner][operator] = approved)
An operator is also allowed to call approve on the signer's positions.
Moves no tokens or ETH. The function is not payable.
formats.shown: "Set operator 0x…" with the intent "Manage FT PUT approvals". The fields show the Operator and 'Access rights' as Grant all / Deny all.

findings.title: setApprovalForAll: interpolatedIntent does not say whether access is granted or revoked, or that it covers all positions.
findings.evidence: descriptor: "interpolatedIntent": "Set operator {operator}", intent "Manage FT PUT approvals". Case 1 renders "Set operator 0xd8dA…6045". The grant is visible only in the 'Access rights: Grant all' field. Code: _operatorApprovals[owner][operator] = approved applies to all of the signer's PUT NFTs.
findings.fix: "interpolatedIntent": "{approved} FT PUT positions to {operator}" with enum values "Grant all"/"Revoke all", or "Set {operator} access to all PUT positions: {approved}"

findings.title: setApprovalForAll: Operator address `types` is limited to contract, but any address can be an operator.
findings.evidence: descriptor: operator.params.types ["contract"]. ERC721Upgradeable._setApprovalForAll rejects only address(0). Case 1 uses an EOA operator.

approve(address to, uint256 tokenId).worst: approve: interpolatedIntent leaves out the operator, though the sentence could carry the address.

setApprovalForAll(address operator, bool.worst: setApprovalForAll: interpolatedIntent does not say whether access is granted or revoked, or that it covers all positions.
